# semester-config - this semester's private config

**PRIVATE (not accessible by enrolled students).**

This is the entire per-semester data hub - instructors manage everything from here: roster and teams, grades, schedule, and this semester's own instructors/TAs. No PII (emails, ids, names) leaves this repo.

Instructors/TAs edit these files; the toolkit's workflows read them and apply the changes automatically. This repo is the SSOT for all semester config.


**Your files and the toolkit's.**
- The files you edit (roster, schedule, semester.yml, grading sheets) are INSTRUCTOR-OWNED - yours. A filled example of each is in the [worked example semester](https://github.com/hertie-data-science-lab/dsl-teaching-toolkit/blob/__CENTRAL_REF__/example-course/semester-org/).
- `.system/` is the toolkit's: its status, its records and the markers that stop anything being sent or graded twice. Leave it alone - deleting a marker repeats what it records.

## `students.csv` - the roster (required)

One row per student. Yours: the engine reads it and writes only one kind of cell in it (a team, below).

| column | notes |
|--------|-------|
| `email` | the **match key** - enrolment codes are mailed here and every other file joins on it |
| `name` | display name |
| `role` | `enrolled` (blank means enrolled) or `auditor` - auditors are read-only: released materials only, no assignment repos, no gradebook, no project teams |
| `team:<n>` | one column per team assignment, `n` its number in `schedule.yml`. A team is the rows sharing a value; blank = no team. Type a team in for `team_formation: assigned`; the Join-team form writes the student's own cell for `self_select` |

Any OTHER column you add (a registrar id, a lecture section, notes) is yours: the engine never reads it.

A push to this file triggers **Sync membership** (the `students` and `auditors` teams, and every project team, follow it; a deleted row revokes access) and **Send enrolment codes** - the only way codes are sent, so adding a row is all it takes. Nobody is ever mailed twice.

## `.system/roster.csv` - who each student is on GitHub (generated)

SYSTEM-OWNED, one row per student, joined to `students.csv` on `email`. Never edit it except to re-point a student who switched GitHub account (their `github_handle`).

| column | written by |
|--------|------------|
| `email` | the student's `students.csv` email |
| `github_handle` | the `join` repo's "Join course" issue |
| `github_id` | the same - the immutable numeric id, which survives a handle rename |
| `enrol_code` | **Send enrolment codes**: a random non-PII token mailed to the student, who pastes it into the "Join course" issue. Never rotated once issued |
| `code_sent_at` | **Send enrolment codes**: when that code email went out. Blank = not yet emailed; clear a cell to re-send |

## `grading_sheets/<assignment>.yml` - marks

One file per assignment, created at handout with every row already in it. It is the ONE
place you type: scores, feedback, an `adjustment_individual` where you need one, a
`late_penalty` (`waive`, or the whole penalty as `15%`) on a late row, and notes that never
leave this repo. Worked examples of both shapes are in the
[worked example semester](https://github.com/hertie-data-science-lab/dsl-teaching-toolkit/blob/__CENTRAL_REF__/example-course/semester-org/grading_sheets).

Everything under `info:` is the toolkit's - when the work came in, how late it was, what
`CONTRIBUTIONS.md` said, the autograde count, and `checked`, the minute the row was last
looked at. It refreshes every quarter of an hour from the
due date and freezes at the cutoff. Everything else is yours and is never touched, including
keys you invent and rows for students who have left. The file is only rewritten when the data
or the header really changed, so your own formatting survives an ordinary tick - but YAML
comments you add are not preserved when a rewrite does happen.

The question names, the `# /N` maxima and the header come from the template's `grading_config.yml`
and this semester's `schedule.yml` and `semester.yml`. Edit them **there** - the sheet's copy is regenerated on
every write.

> ### Changing a grade
>
> Retype it and re-run **Distribute grades**. Nothing is said twice, so only that student is
> reached. To recompute an autograde count, delete `.system/autograde/<slug>/`.

### What reaches students, when

**Nothing here reaches a student until you run Distribute grades.** It writes each
student's private `grades-<handle>` gradebook - the one place a mark or a feedback line ever
goes - and `.system/semester-grades.csv` (the semester grades file - generated, never hand-edited), and
records every gradebook and email in `.system/gradebook/distributed.csv`. That file is SYSTEM-owned:
it is what stops a re-run repeating itself and what lets a failed notification be retried.

## `.system/assignments.lock.yml` - what the Join-team form is allowed to do (generated)

SYSTEM-OWNED, and the one file here nobody edits. The "Join team" workflow runs in the PUBLIC `join` repo, under a token that cannot reach an assignment template or the course's defaults, so it cannot work out how an assignment runs. This file mirrors the answers it needs - `team_formation` and `max_team_size` (set on the assignment's `schedule.yml` entry, else this repo's `semester.yml` `defaults:`, else the course's `course.yml` `defaults:`), and whether team formation is open for that assignment right now (`team_formation_window`, with the day it shuts in `team_formation_closes`, and the assignment's page on the semester site in `team_formation_page`) - one entry per assignment in `schedule.yml`.

It is rewritten by the quarter-hourly **Scheduled release** tick - which is what opens and shuts the window on its own clock - and again by **Sync membership** (which a push to `schedule.yml` triggers), by every **Release assignment**, and by the nightly **Refresh actions**. Change an assignment's shape in its own `grading_config.yml` on the template's `solution` branch, and how this semester runs it on its `schedule.yml` entry or in `semester.yml`; this file catches up on the next sync. An assignment whose template does not exist yet is locked to `none`, so no team can be formed for it until the template says what it is.

## `.system/team-formation/mailed.csv` - who has already been emailed about forming a team (generated)

SYSTEM-OWNED, and nobody edits it. One row per message the scheduler has sent (`assignment, recipient, phase, mailed_at`): it is what stops the hourly tick emailing the same student twice, and what lets a message that could not be sent be retried on the next one. Delete a row and that message goes out again.

## `schedule.yml` - the release plan + due dates + events (optional)

This semester's whole schedule in one file. Changing a date later is just committing the edit to this file on main (via the GitHub web UI, or a local clone/commit/push).

## `semester.yml` - this semester's people, defaults and student site

- `people:` - this semester's instructors and TAs, one list, each with a `role:`. **Sync membership** reconciles them into this semester's own `instructors` team AND a course-org level `instructors-<semester>` team (push on every course-org repo this semester's `schedule.yml` names, plus the course `.github` repo so they can use the workflows too). They are also the student site's instructor cards and the people a fault here is mailed to.
- `defaults:` - the late window and penalty, team formation and size, repo visibility, timezone, archive grace and default materials repo for this semester. Every key is seeded commented, with the value it inherits (from the course's `course.yml`, else the institution) beside it; uncomment to override. An assignment's own `schedule.yml` entry overrides these in turn.
- `student_site:` - `syllabus:`, the released file the site's home page pins.
